feedback: Before this geometry races, the evidence is as follows. In iteration 2 (0.09 m track), line loss was 0 on the oval and s-bend and progress rose to 0.44 on the oval, but oval steering_oscillation rose to 0.272 from 0.173 at iteration 1 (0.12 m track). That is the yaw-gain trade: a narrower track gives more turn per command. In iteration 1, max_error stayed at 0.0619 m with a 7-sensor, 16 mm array, so sensing is not the limit. In iteration 2 max_error stayed at 0.063 m, so the controller or reaction point remains the limit. I am widening the track to 0.10 m and holding the controller fixed to test that trade in isolation. Next race: if oval steering_oscillation falls below about 0.2 while progress holds near 0.4, keep 0.10 m and test the reaction point. If oscillation is still above 0.2, the gain is still too high for the track, so widen to 0.11 m or accept a lower kp. If max_error stays at 0.062 m with oscillation under 0.2, move the sensor row to y = 0.02 m.
requested_changes: If oval steering_oscillation is still above 0.2 after the 0.10 m track (iteration 2 was 0.272, iteration 1 at 0.12 m was 0.173): widen wheel_track to 0.11 m, since the yaw per command falls as the track widens.

If max_error stays near 0.062 m with line_loss_events at 0 and steering_oscillation below 0.2 (iterations 1 and 2 both show about 0.062 to 0.063 m): move the sensor row from y = 0.03 m to y = 0.02 m, because the reaction point rather than the sensors is the limit.

If progress falls below about 0.35 on the oval at 0.10 m (iteration 1 at 0.12 m gave 0.31 and iteration 2 at 0.09 m gave 0.44): try wheel_radius 0.035 m, because speed limits progress and the wheel radius is the lever for it.
